stem.text: A particle moves along the curve \( x y + y^{2} = 6 \) so that its coordinates \( x \) and \( y \) are differentiable functions of time \( t \). At the instant the particle is at the point \( (1, 2) \), \( \frac{dx}{dt} = 5 \) units per second. Find \( \frac{dy}{dt} \), in units per second, at that instant.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate both sides of \( x y + y^{2} = 6 \) with respect to \( t \), using the product rule on the term that contains both variables: \( \left(y\right)\frac{dx}{dt} + \left(x + 2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \).
At \( (1, 2) \) the coefficient of \( \frac{dx}{dt} \) is \( 2 \) and the coefficient of \( \frac{dy}{dt} \) is \( 5 \). Substitute \( \frac{dx}{dt} = 5 \): \( (2)(5) + (5)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \).
